I'll think through this as the farmer would, then give the plan.

---

My name isn't important. I'm 50, been on this land since I was twenty. Primary school is all I had — my father pulled me out to help in the field. But thirty years of farming teaches you plenty.

I have 7.8 mu. Last year I put about 6 mu into the wheat-maize rotation like always — that's my main income. The other 1.8 mu I keep in cotton, on the strip near the road where the soil is a bit sandier and wheat doesn't do as well there. My father grew cotton on that patch too.

**Wheat** (planted last October, coming up now):
I used the same as last year — before sowing I spread about 2 bags of compound fertilizer (50 kg bags, the 15-15-15 kind my brother-in-law at the agri-shop sells) per mu, and then at spring green-up I top-dress with about 20 kg of urea per mu. That comes out to roughly 17 kg of nitrogen, 7.5 of phosphorus, 7.5 of potassium per mu. My neighbor Old Wang uses a little less urea but his yield is always lower than mine, so I stick with my amount. I irrigate after green-up, at jointing, and again at grain-filling — three times from the well. I use improved wheat seed, Jimai variety, saved some from last year and bought some new. Last year I got about 480 kg/mu, so I expect similar. I'll spray once for aphids in April, once for rust if I see it — usually two sprays.

**Maize** (I'll plant in June right after wheat harvest):
I no-till directly into the wheat stubble with the rented seeder — saves labor and time, everyone in the village does it this way now. I use Zhengdan hybrid seed, costs more but the yield is worth it. At sowing I put about 1 bag of compound fertilizer per mu as base, then at the big-trumpet stage (around knee-high) I top-dress 25 kg of urea per mu. That's about 19 kg N, 7.5 P, 7.5 K. Maybe I put a bit too much urea but I'd rather have the yield — a bad maize year hurts more than a bag of fertilizer costs. Two irrigations usually — at sowing and at tasseling. I spray for corn borer once, maybe twice if the moths are heavy. Last year maize was about 550 kg/mu.

**Cotton** (1.8 mu, planting late April):
Cotton is more work but the price has been okay lately. I use improved seed from the county station. Cotton eats more fertilizer than grain — I put 2 bags of compound at planting and top-dress urea twice, maybe 15 kg each time. So about 20 kg N, 8 P, 8 K per mu. Cotton needs more spraying — bollworm, aphids, spider mites — I usually spray 6 or 7 times through the season, can't skip or I lose the bolls. Two irrigations, at squaring and at boll-setting. I plough the cotton ground before planting, it's not like the wheat-maize rotation. Last year cotton gave me around 230 kg/mu of seed cotton.

I don't waste money, but I don't cut corners on fertilizer either. My wife says I buy too much urea. But if the wheat is yellow in March it's too late to fix. Better safe.
